transcript: Like flowers, azelaic acid and tretinoin is a great combination, but a lot of people get the timing wrong. It's not about using them together, it's about splitting them in the same routine. One goes on in your morning routine and the other at night. And here is why. Apply your azelaic acid in the morning, then layer with your moisturizer and sunscreen. Azelaic acid is gentle enough for daytime use and won't necessarily make you more sensitive to the sun. At night is when your retinol or tretinoin comes in. Start with a pea size amount just a few times a week and follow with a moisturizer to buffer any irritation as your skin adjusts. So the bottom line is azelaic acid by day, tretinoin or retinoid by night, and sunscreen no matter what.

title: How to get rid of DEEP acne scars?
caption:
Scrubbing won't erase sunken, atrophic acne scars caused by lost collagen. Control active breakouts first with a topical retinoid, then see a dermatologist for targeted treatments like subcision, TCA cross, or lasers.

Brought to you by  @cerave .
transcript: If you have these deep scars in your skin, you might think you can just scrub them away. Please don't, because these aren't just dog spots or marks. They're actually acne scars called atrophic scars, meaning it's underneath your skin. This usually happens when you have a deep inflamed pimple and your skin doesn't make enough collagen while it heals. So when the pimple goes away, your skin underneath can sink in, leaving you with a dent in your skin. Now you don't want to treat the acne scars if you're still breaking out, because you're trying to fix the damage while your skin is still creating more. Instead, you want to get your acne under control first. And you can start with a topical retinoid, because this helps prevent new breakouts and post-acne marks. And when you're left with the deep scars, a dermatologist can help with precise treatments, such as chemical peels, subsision, or laser research.

title: What To Know Before Getting A CO2 Laser Skin Treatment
caption:
CO2 and Erbium lasers are powerful tools for total skin resurfacing, effectively targeting deep wrinkles, discoloration, and uneven texture by removing the damaged outer layers of the skin. While the rejuvenating results can be incredibly long-lasting—especially when paired with a solid skincare routine—these treatments require a serious commitment to healing.

In this video, we cover the exact benefits of ablative lasers, the expected downtime, and why choosing an experienced surgeon or dermato
transcript: CO2 and erbium lasers are really powerful, game-changing lasers that I get asked about a lot. And the reason why, in general, they're so powerful is because think of them almost like a lawnmower. Think of it as as your skin being the, you know, the lawn and these ablative CO2 and erbium wavelengths are coming through and removing a portion of the top layer of the skin. So, with it goes the stratum corneum, which is that dull layer of dead surface skin. Then comes the epithelium, the top layer of the skin that sometimes fine lines and wrinkles show up at, pigmentation shows up, and it even can go as deep as the upper portion of the dermis. So, what you do in response to that laser is you're getting a whole new layer of skin that flourishes and grows through. So, this total skin resurfacing that you get by removing those outer layers gives you an all-around rejuvenation. Wrinkles, discoloration, and even texture. The downside, there is always a catch, right? So, you're going to get this beautiful rejuvenation, skin's going to look amazing. The downside is that it A, it's not permanent, although it is definitely longer-lasting. I mean, by the time those deep lines around the top lip starts to reform, it could be literally years if maybe it's a one-and-done even. And if you use proper skin care on top of it after you get this done, a lot of the changes are going to persist because you've gotten this massive momentum shift going forward with this ablative laser. Now, the catch is, unfortunately, they're generally expensive. They have a significant downtime associated with it, anywhere from a week to 3 weeks. And if you are getting this done by somebody who doesn't really know what they're doing, huge huge risk because there's a risk of burning, there's a risk of discoloration, hypopigmentation, a number of other things. So, this is a procedure that you want to get done by an experienced surgeon or dermatologist. This is not a med spa procedure that should be done, generally speaking, by, say a nurse or an aesthetician, etc. So, again, overall game-changing procedure for the right person with the advanced sign of skin aging, but it requires a serious commitment both to healing and finding an expert provider.
